clue.text: Unable to stop notice passed around court

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement, a notice

indicators.note: passed is placed around court, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to pass away is to die, so passed gives DIED

explanation.surface: Someone can't stop themselves passing a notice round the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked on a habit is unable to quit it, which is what being addicted means.

clue.text: A supporter rounds on a spaceman

indicators.note: rounds means goes around, so the support encloses the other words

parts.note: a strut is a structural support

explanation.surface: A backer turns on a space traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller trained to fly on spacecraft.

clue.text: Point to powder coating sheep

indicators.note: the powder coats, so it lies around the sheep

parts.note: dust is fine powder
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: Instructions to dust a sheep with powder.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point, directly toward where the sun sets.

clue.text: Out to lunch, map makers taking shelter from squall

indicators.note: the map piece sits inside the squall, sheltering within it

parts.note: a squall is a loud cry, as of a baby
the A-Z is the classic London street atlas

explanation.surface: Cartographers on a lunch break duck in out of a sudden storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squall' looks like a storm but is a bawl. The A-Z is a well-known British street-map book.
explanation.definitionFit: Out to lunch is slang for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Woeful serenade about depression finished thus?

indicators.note: the jumbled song wraps around the depression
woeful suggests a badly done version, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: a dint is a dent or hollow

explanation.surface: A sad love song about depression ends as you might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woeful' looks like it describes the song's mood, but it is the anagram signal; the question mark marks the definition as a playful guess at the outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A woeful serenade about depression could only conclude with crying, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Black convict's problem after long-distance transfer

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour
an old lag is slang for a habitual convict

explanation.surface: A black convict faces trouble after being moved a long way to another prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('s = is) between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness and disorientation after a long flight across time zones is a familiar travel complaint.

clue.text: Newspaper article occupies retired collier

indicators.note: the article occupies space inside the other word

parts.note: a former coal miner is an ex-miner
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news story fills a page about a retired coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper article' looks like one phrase but splits into definition and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Several newspapers carry this title, such as the San Francisco and Irish papers.

clue.text: Lost expression "going into retreat"

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lost in sports results tables
airing views is expressing them

explanation.surface: A forgotten phrase about withdrawing from the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den, a retreat, so this means heading into a den.

clue.text: Great one in 3 age group

indicators.note: the answer at 3 down means mad, so it signals that these letters go wild

explanation.surface: A major figure in a particular age bracket.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is the answer to 3 down, which means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: People born and living at about the same time form a single cohort.

clue.text: He (or she) keeps date with comic

indicators.note: the pronoun holds the other pieces within it, as a box keeps its contents

parts.note: they is the gender-neutral pronoun standing for he or she
and is a synonym of with, as in bread with butter

explanation.surface: A person keeps a romantic date and brings along a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long-running British children's comic magazine, home of Desperate Dan.

clue.text: See 8
I'll forget stupid racist banter

indicators.note: stupid suggests nonsense, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A person vows to forget some dumb, bigoted talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A forgetful, disorganised person might say this of themselves, so the phrase describes one.

clue.text: Born through love, you would like Cyclops

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
née marks a woman's maiden name: born as
ye'd is an old contraction of 'ye would'

explanation.surface: Something born of love that you would compare with the mythical giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Love's O comes first, then NEE: 'through' is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclopes of Greek myth had a single eye in the middle of the forehead.

clue.text: Using club, short hit to where hole is?

definitions.text: Using club, short hit to where hole is?

parts.note: a chip is a short lofted golf shot played with a club
a ball that drops is in the hole

explanation.surface: A golfer takes a club and plays a short shot towards the hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the description of the shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a chip shot that drops straight into the cup is called this.

clue.text: Leaderless team affected?

indicators.note: leaderless means losing the head, the opening letter

parts.note: a party is a group of people working together, a team

explanation.surface: A team without a captain wonders whether it has been hurt by the loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentiously showy about artistic taste is what arty describes, like affected behaviour.

clue.text: As a big group, rent things out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A large crowd hires stuff out.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving in large numbers, as a crowd or a force, is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: House of station manager receives recycled books

indicators.note: the manager takes in the books, holding them inside

parts.note: a head is the person in charge, a manager

indicators.note: recycled means the letters go round, the first moved to the back

parts.note: tomes are large books

explanation.surface: A station manager's home takes in books for reuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' moves the T of TOMES to the end, giving OMEST. A station is an Australian ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: The main farmhouse on an Australian sheep or cattle station has this name.

clue.text: Rodent's sleeping place on river

parts.note: a dorm is a dormitory, a room for sleeping
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A rodent's bed lies on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A small nocturnal rodent famous for hibernating.

clue.text: Nothing connected in the car but new rev counter

indicators.note: in places the joined pieces inside the rearranged letters
new signals that the letters of 'the car' are made anew, rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
met means came together, connected

explanation.surface: Nothing has been wired up in a brand-new car except the rev counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges THE CAR into TACHER, and 'in' puts O plus MET inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This dashboard instrument measures engine speed in revolutions per minute.

clue.text: Father's old hat in fashion

indicators.note: in places the old hat within the priest

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest, Father; the 's is has
something out is out of fashion, old hat

explanation.surface: Dad's old hat is back in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father's' reads as possessive but means CURE has OUT in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Haute couture is high fashion, the design of clothes.

clue.text: Crash barrier

definitions.meaning: a floating barrier across a harbour or river mouth

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a deep bang and also a beam or chain blocking a waterway.

clue.text: Cops see daring crook's heading to centre

indicators.note: the heading, first letter, travels to the middle of the word

parts.note: bold means daring
crook is Australian slang for ill

explanation.surface: Police see a brave criminal heading downtown.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLDILL has its first letter B shifted to the middle, the fourth of seven. The Old Bill is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British slang for the police force as a whole.

clue.text: Would one count as peak period?

definitions.meaning: one who adds numbers, a person who sums
the hottest season, the high point of the year

explanation.surface: Asking whether a time of highest demand qualifies.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as sum-mer it is someone who counts; it is also the warmest season, peak holiday time.

clue.text: Queen will eat fish too

indicators.note: eating takes the fish inside the queen

parts.note: Good Queen Bess was Elizabeth I
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: The monarch is going to have fish as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and in addition are synonyms of both words, as in 'there were others too'.

clue.text: Teacher bathed one

parts.note: swam means went bathing in water
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A teacher went swimming, alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious teacher is called a swami.

clue.text: In cowhouse, dairymaid was milking

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dairymaid was milking cows in the cowshed.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk someone is to exploit them, just as to use them is.

clue.text: Can it give info about some Africans?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the info is placed around the people

parts.note: SP, starting price, is British slang for the information on something
the Hutu are a people of Rwanda and Burundi

explanation.surface: Asks whether a tin can tell us about certain African peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a tin, but 'Can it' is slang for be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are blunt slang orders to stop talking.

clue.text: Nirvana single's featured in show

indicators.note: featured in puts the single's letters within the show

parts.note: a parade is a display or show
single is I (one), and 's stands for is: I plus S

explanation.surface: A single by the band Nirvana is featured in a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Nirvana looks like the grunge band, but here it is the state of bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a state of perfect bliss or heavenly happiness.

clue.text: To grow, comedian has to write

parts.note: Jack Dee is a British stand-up comedian
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A comic has to write in order to develop.
explanation.definitionFit: To intensify or become greater, as a feeling deepens, is to grow.

clue.text: One out of time ruled a commoner

indicators.note: out of means the unit is outside, around the time

parts.note: a unit is one single thing
led means ruled or governed

explanation.surface: A lone figure from another era ruled over a commoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' puts UNIT around T, giving UNTIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A commoner holds no title of nobility, so is without a title.
